{{Short description|Annual screenwriting award}}{{Unreliable sources|date=June 2026|imdb=y}}{{Infobox award | name = Writers Guild of America Award for Adapted Screenplay | image = Paul Thomas Anderson - BFI Southbank.jpg | image_upright = 0.7 | caption = The 2025 winner: Paul Thomas Anderson | awarded_for = Outstanding Writing for a Film Adapted from Another Medium | presenter = [[Writers Guild of America]] | country = United States | year = 1970 | holder = [[Paul Thomas Anderson]], ''[[One Battle After Another]]'' ([[78th Writers Guild of America Awards|2025]]) | website = http://www.wga.org/ }} The '''Writers Guild of America Award for Best Adapted Screenplay''' is one of the three [[screenwriting]] [[Writers Guild of America Award]]s, focused specifically for film. The [[Writers Guild of America]] began making the distinction between an original screenplay and an [[Film adaptation|adapted screenplay]] in [[22nd Writers Guild of America Awards|1970]], when [[Waldo Salt]], screenwriter for ''Midnight Cowboy'', won for "Best Adapted Drama" and [[Arnold Schulman]] won "Best Adapted Comedy" for his screenplay of ''[[Goodbye, Columbus (film)|Goodbye, Columbus]]''.{{cite web|url=http://www.wga.org/awards/awardssub.aspx?id=1551|title=Past Winners|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061001153001/http://www.wga.org/awards/awardssub.aspx?id=1551|archive-date=October 1, 2006|access-date=2008-04-21|url-status=dead}} Separate awards for dramas and comedies continued [[1984 in film|until 1984]]. ==Winners and nominees== * † indicates an [[Academy Award for Best Adapted Screenplay]] winner ===1960s=== {| class="wikitable" width="95%" ! width="5%" |Year ! width="30%" |Film ! width="30%" |Recipient(s) ! width="35%" |Source material |- | rowspan="12" style="text-align:center;" | [[1969 in film|1969]]
